festivals: Rath Yatra (Lokotsav; on Ashadha Shukla Dwitiya, same day as Puri)

history.period: Established ~450 years ago (16th century; Rath Yatra since 1878)
history.summary: Established about 450 years ago by Sadhu Sarangdasji on the banks of the Sabarmati at Jamalpur; the site began as a Hanuman shrine founded by his predecessor Hanumandasji, to which the Jagannath-Balabhadra-Subhadra idols were added. The annual Rath Yatra, begun in 1878 by Mahant Narsinhdasji, is the third-largest in India after Puri and Kolkata and is celebrated as Gujarat's Lokotsav: elephants lead the procession, the Gujarat Chief Minister performs the Pahind Vidhi, the ~14-16 km route passes through the old city, and the procession halts at Saraspur for the traditional Maha Bhoj community feast. The temple complex was renovated 1996-2000, with the deities reinstalled on a raised Ratna Vedi and a large auditorium added. It is run by the Shree Jagannathji Mandir Trust Committee.

town_description: Ahmedabad is Gujarat's largest city and its former capital, founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmed Shah I on the banks of the Sabarmati river. Its walled old city became India's first UNESCO World Heritage City in 2017, known for carved wooden havelis, pols, stepwells, and Sultanate-era monuments. Today it is a major industrial and commercial hub, famous for its food culture, the Sabarmati Ashram, and as the gateway to Gujarat.
